title: 2.3L EcoBoost Cooling Component Map
introduction:
The turbocharger gets a place on this coolant map too. I start at the radiator on the left, then trace the connections toward the engine block and cylinder head in the center and right. The turbocharger branch sits above the radiator, and the heater-core route stretches across the upper right. Thinking of these as branches of the same plumbing network makes the hose spaghetti considerably less mysterious.

Match each drawing callout to the accompanying table, then follow the thin connecting lines and small arrowheads across the gaps. The turbocharger inlet and outlet tubes shown here belong to its coolant circuit; this is not an intake-air routing diagram. Around the engine, distinguish the radiator-return route from the bypass and heater branches by tracing their connections rather than choosing a hose by color alone.

Colors identify illustrated coolant-temperature bands under the conditions in the note. This reference teaches component identification and how to follow the drawing; it does not supply filling, bleeding, access, replacement or diagnostic procedures. The separated parts do not represent a removal order.

edits.text: NOTE: Coolant temperature changes with ambient temperature and engine load. This drawing uses an ambient temperature of 38° C (100° F). Red arrows show coolant over 90° C (194° F); orange arrows show coolant at approximately 90° C (194° F); blue arrows show coolant below 90° C (194° F).
edits.why: The arrows describe the same coolant at different temperature bands along the illustrated routes. They do not mark different fluids or establish a universal fault threshold.
